newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN weaker but off lows after big H1 loss.
newsitem.headline: GAN weaker but off lows after big H1 loss.

text.p: French state-controlled insurer GAN was down 2.47 percent but off lows touched earlier in the day after it reported a nearly a billion franc first-half loss.
At 1355 GMT, the share was trading down three francs at 118.5 francs in volume of 98,594 shares.
Earlier in the day it had been down more than six percent.

The insurer reported its net consolidated loss for the six months to end June ballooned to 965 million francs from a loss of 387 million francs a year earlier. The loss was mainly from its property banking activities.
It warned the market it would show a loss for the year but said it would not necessarily be double the first half loss.
GAN's property woes aside, analysts said the performance by its core insurance activities showed a good improvement.
"The insurance results are in light with what was expected. They're even good," said analyst Jerome Labin of French brokerage Pinatton.
He said, however, that he was lowering his forecast for full year 1996, predicting a loss of two billion francs instead of a loss of 300 million francs.
